extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO disciplinary stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural rules governing professional conduct, disciplinary violations, and sanctions for practitioners who practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act with reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. § 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client (37 C.F.R. § 11.103).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete failures treated as violations include: failing to file acceptable drawings and pay required filing fees; failing to file a reply to a Notice to File Missing Parts; allowing an application to go abandoned without the client's knowledge or permission; failing to file required application paperwork or establish entitlement to reduced fees; and failing to file required replies to USPTO decisions (examples (i)–(vi) in the Joint Legal Conclusions). Repeated or systemic failures to timely perform prosecutorial tasks are evidence of lack of diligence/promptness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep clients reasonably informed about status (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall keep clients reasonably informed about the status of a matter (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of violations: not informing a client that a Notice to File Missing Parts was issued, not informing a client that a Notice of Abandonment issued, not notifying a client that an application was filed without required documents. Keeping clients informed includes timely communication of significant filings, deadlines, and adverse events that affect the client's rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptly comply with reasonable client requests for information (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative failures: repeatedly refusing or failing to provide a filing receipt upon request, failing to provide a copy of a Notice to File Missing Parts as requested, failing to respond to inquiries about the status of a petition. Prompt compliance with documentation and status requests is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain matters sufficiently for client decision-making (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions regarding the representation (37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations include failing to advise clients of options and potential consequences of not responding to Notices to File Missing Parts or Decisions on Petition, failing to explain consequences of abandonment and possibility of revival, and failing to explain alternatives or next steps when required. Explanations should enable informed client choices about remedies, withdrawals, and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptly deliver funds to entitled third persons (37 C.F.R. § 11.115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall promptly deliver to a third person any funds the third person is entitled to receive (37 C.F.R. § 11.115(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: accepting client-paid USPTO filing fees and neither paying them to the USPTO nor promptly returning them to the client constitutes a violation. Practitioners must segregate and timely disburse funds to the proper payee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect client’s interest upon withdrawal (37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall protect a client’s interest upon withdrawal (37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included conduct: promptly returning unearned or advanced client funds and taking steps so the client is not prejudiced by withdrawal. Failure to return advanced USPTO fees or otherwise safeguard client rights when withdrawing is a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the order: accepting patent application fees and neither paying those fees to the USPTO nor returning the fees to the client; failing to inform a client that an application had gone abandoned. Misrepresentation includes affirmative deceit and withholding material facts from clients where duty to disclose exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior public discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not be publicly disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior public reprimand or other public discipline by a state authority is itself a violation under § 11.804(h) and is an aggravating factor in subsequent USPTO disciplinary proceedings (the order cites a Nevada public reprimand as a basis for violation and sanction consideration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and applicability of USPTO discipline (35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D), 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over registered patent practitioners and disciplinary proceedings pursuant to specified statutes and rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered practitioners before the USPTO are subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101–11.901) and to discipline under the cited statutes/regulations. The order identifies the statutory/regulatory basis for institution and approval of settlement agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate with OED investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner is expected to cooperate during investigations by the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to cooperate with OED's investigation is an adverse factor considered in determining sanctions (the order notes Respondent failed to cooperate and OED considered that in imposing discipline). Cooperation includes responding to OED inquiries and providing requested documents/information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in sanctioning (prior warnings, remorse, aggravating/mitigating factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED considers prior warnings, prior discipline, cooperation, acknowledgment/remorse, and other factors when determining appropriate sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order notes that prior warnings about diligence and communication, failure to cooperate, acknowledgment of wrongdoing and expressed remorse were considered in reaching the settlement. Prior disciplinary history and the nature/extent of misconduct are relevant aggravating/mitigating factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary outcomes and reinstatement conditions (suspension, probation, limited recognition, CLE, OED procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible disciplinary sanctions include suspension from practice, probationary conditions, limited recognition to conclude pending matters, publication of the Final Order, and conditions for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specific order imposed: nine (9) months suspension; probation commencing on the date of the Final Order and terminating 24 months after a decision granting reinstatement; 30-day limited recognition to conclude pending matters; as a condition of reinstatement, completion of six (6) hours CLE on law office management for solo/small practitioners; OED may issue an Order to Show Cause and seek additional suspension (procedures and 15‑day response timeline); the practitioner waived rights to reconsideration/review/appeal; the Final Order will be published in the OED FOIA Reading Room and a notice in the Official Gazette. These components illustrate the procedural mechanics and typical conditions attached to discipline and reinstatement.
